description:
Tier 2 on paper, but the [u8]-only versions work today (image_blur already does a 3x3 blur on raw RGB). Anchors: image/vix (libvips), cvt_color (RGB888 to RGB565/666 for Nerves displays, hand-written C++ with optional OpenMP), dither (error diffusion for e-paper). The jobs: bilinear and Lanczos-3 resize of raw RGB/RGBA frames, RGB<->YUV420 conversion, Floyd-Steinberg dithering to 1-bit. libvips is SIMD-tuned (orc/highway), so resize is expected poor against it on speed; cvt_color and dither references are plain loops, parity expected, and on Nerves there is no libvips.

Kernels: `resize_bilinear(px :: [u8], w, h, ch, out_w, out_h) :: [u8]`, `resize_lanczos3(...)` with weights precomputed per output column/row into alloc'd [f64] arrays (separable: horizontal pass then vertical), `rgb_to_yuv420(px, w, h) :: [u8]`, `rgb888_to_rgb565(px) :: [u8]` (needs bsr/band: defk-w38), `dither_fs(gray :: [u8], w, h) :: [u8]` with an [i64] error row.

Elixir baselines: pure Elixir binary comprehensions for each (first pass, then optimise with :binary.part-based row access); report libvips beside.

Realistic size: 1080p frames (6 MB) and 320x240 (Nerves). Expected verdict: good vs pure Elixir for all; poor vs libvips on resize; parity with cvt_color.

Needs: nothing for bilinear/Lanczos/YUV/dither; defk-w38 for RGB565; defk-4ai ([f32] weights) is optional. 2D indexing is row*w+col arithmetic with range facts: check the fast-path report for which bounds checks stayed (defk-6cn).

Done when: agreement with the pure Elixir versions holds (bit-exact for integer paths; Lanczos float rounding documented), verdicts measured, README rows added.
title: Image resize, colour conversion and dithering from scratch vs image/vix (libvips) and cvt_color
